<body>

<a href="#main" class="skip-link">Skip to main content</a>

<div class="page-layout">
  <nav class="side-nav" aria-label="Section navigation">
    <ol>
      <li><a href="#overview">Overview</a></li>
      <li><a href="#contributions">Contributions</a></li>
      <li><a href="#method">Method</a></li>
      <li><a href="#results">Results</a></li>
      <li><a href="#figures">Figures</a></li>
      <li><a href="#limitations">Limitations</a></li>
    </ol>
  </nav>

  <div class="content-col">
    <main id="main">

      <section id="overview">
        <h1>Specificity and Causality Audits for Activation-Based Safety Readouts</h1>
        <p class="tldr">
          Can you tell whether a language model is safe by reading its internal activations,
          without running a full behavioural benchmark? We tested 32 candidate readouts against
          model modifications that provably do not change safety behaviour. On 24 such no-op edits
          across three model families, mid-layer activation readouts produced zero false alarms;
          the standard logit-gap baseline produced 11 (McNemar <i>p</i>&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.001). A causal
          intervention grid on Qwen3-4B then showed that the refusal direction is linearly readable
          from activations but removing it at any single site does not change the model's judged
          refusal: it rewrites its refusal in different words. No second-order readout survived
          blind held-out confirmation at the pre-registered bar, and the effective rank of the score
          matrix (7.2) rules out reducing all readouts to a single number.
        </p>
        <div class="hero-links">
          <a href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-f8532e-safety-only-checks-output-when-warned@main/paper.pdf">Read the paper (PDF)</a>
          <a href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-f8532e-safety-only-checks-output-when-warned">Code repository</a>
        </div>
      </section>

      <section id="contributions">
        <h2>Contributions</h2>
        <div class="contributions-grid">
          <div class="contribution">
            <h3>Activation readouts have far fewer false alarms than the logit baseline</h3>
            <p>
              On 24 behaviourally graded no-op edits spanning numerical precision, identity
              transforms, non-safety adaptation and head-only edits, geometric activation readouts
              produce zero false alarms while the final-layer logit gap produces 11 (exact McNemar
              <i>p</i>&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.001). On the core 15-pair panel, mid-layer readouts fire on
              at most 3 no-ops; the logit baseline fires on 6&ndash;8.
            </p>
          </div>
          <div class="contribution">
            <h3>The refusal direction is decodable but causally inert at the prompt site</h3>
            <p>
              In a 6-band &times; 3-site causal grid, removing the refusal direction at the last
              prompt token does not change judged refusal in any of 18 cells
              (max&nbsp;|effect|&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.056, TOST
              <i>p</i>&nbsp;&lt;&nbsp;10<sup>&minus;23</sup>). The model rewrites its refusal in
              different words. The causal lever is over-refusal on benign-borderline prompts.
            </p>
          </div>
          <div class="contribution">
            <h3>Abliteration both rotates and shrinks the refusal representation</h3>
            <p>
              Global removal of the refusal direction at band B4 reduces instruct refusal from
              0.92 to 0.67; SafeRL resists with a difference-in-differences of +0.23
              [0.08,&nbsp;0.38]. The cross-model cosine drops from 0.999 at B1 to 0.31 at B5,
              and N1 and N6 drop by 71% and 57% from instruct to the abliterated checkpoint.
            </p>
          </div>
          <div class="contribution">
            <h3>Second-order readouts index trade-off position, not safety level</h3>
            <p>
              Fifteen candidate readouts are screened on 48 checkpoints; none of 11 survivors
              passes blind held-out confirmation. Every readout sign is inverted relative to its
              registered prediction: they track where a model sits on the
              refusal&ndash;permissiveness spectrum, not a safety level per se. The effective
              rank of the score matrix is 7.2, ruling out a one-coordinate summary.
            </p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </section>

      <section id="method">
        <h2>Method</h2>
        <figure class="method-fig">
          <img src="figures/fig_overview_v0.jpg"
               alt="Flowchart of the three-experiment design: Experiment 1 grades parent-child model pairs as NOOP or EFFECTIVE then scores 32 readouts for false alarms and sensitivity; Experiment 2 runs a 6-band by 3-site causal grid on Qwen3-4B variants; Experiment 3 screens 15 second-order readouts on 48 checkpoints and tests survivors on 12 blind held-out checkpoints.">
          <figcaption>
            Overview of the three-experiment design. Experiment 1 (left): parent checkpoints are
            modified, each pair is behaviourally graded, then 32 candidate readouts are scored.
            Experiment 2 (centre): a causal intervention grid tests whether removing the refusal
            direction changes judged refusal. Experiment 3 (right): 15 second-order readouts are
            screened and tested on a blind held-out panel.
          </figcaption>
        </figure>

        <p>
          All three experiments share the same behavioural grading pipeline. Each checkpoint is
          evaluated on 85 harmful prompts and 83 benign prompts with an LLM judge (Gemini 2.5 Flash
          Lite; split-half reliability 0.96 for harmful compliance, 0.94 for over-refusal).
          Behavioural labels are frozen before any readout is computed, enforced by a SHA-256 hash
          chain.
        </p>

        <h3>Experiment 1: Specificity Audit</h3>
        <p>
          Parent&ndash;child model pairs are constructed across three families (Qwen3-0.6B,
          Llama-3.2-1B, Falcon3-1B) with modifications in four categories: numerical precision
          (8 pairs), identity transforms (2), non-safety adaptation (2) and head-only edits (3).
          Behavioural grading yields 15 no-ops and 9 effective changes. For each pair, 32 candidate
          readouts are computed from residual-stream activations, logits, weights and text outputs. A
          readout fires a false alarm if its paired-bootstrap CI excludes zero in the expected
          direction on a no-op pair.
        </p>

        <h3>Experiment 2: Causal Intervention Grid</h3>
        <p>
          Three Qwen3-4B variants (Instruct, SafeRL, abliterated) are tested in a grid crossing
          six depth bands (B1&ndash;B6, each one-sixth of the 36-layer stack) with three
          intervention sites: last prompt token (P), first decode positions (D'), and the early
          response window (E). Each cell runs five arms including a matched random control. A cell
          counts as causal only if the treatment differs from the random control after
          Holm&ndash;Bonferroni correction at &alpha;&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.05 over all 18 cells.
        </p>

        <h3>Experiment 3: Second-Order Readout Screen</h3>
        <p>
          Fifteen candidates measuring write-handle redundancy (W1&ndash;W8), dimensionless geometry
          (G1&ndash;G4) and competing mechanisms (A1&ndash;A3) are screened on 48 checkpoints from
          7 lineages. Four are dropped for collinearity with the logit baseline. The remaining 11
          are tested on 12 blind held-out checkpoints from 7 non-overlapping lineages. Confirmation
          requires the candidate's correlation with over-refusal to exceed the logit baseline by a
          margin whose CI excludes zero.
        </p>
      </section>

      <section id="results">
        <h2>Results</h2>

        <div class="result-block">
          <div class="result-label">Experiment 1 &mdash; Specificity</div>
          <div class="result-num">0 vs 11 <span class="unit">false alarms on 24 no-op edits (McNemar <i>p</i> = 0.001)</span></div>
          <p>
            Geometric activation readouts produce zero false alarms on the pooled 24-pair set; the
            logit-gap baseline produces 11. On the core 15-pair panel, the best activation readouts
            fire on at most 3 no-ops, while the logit gap fires on 6&ndash;8 out of 15. The
            weight-space cosine B7 fires on 9 of 15: every dtype cast triggers it.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div class="result-block">
          <div class="result-label">Displacement mechanism</div>
          <div class="result-num">6.2&times; <span class="unit">displacement ratio (logit 0.150 vs activation 0.024 null SD)</span></div>
          <p>
            The logit gap operates at the decision boundary where small perturbations produce large
            score changes. Mid-layer activation readouts measure the geometry of the representation
            space, which is more stable under numerical-precision and identity modifications.
            Final-layer logits amplify implementation-irrelevant variation.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div class="result-block">
          <div class="result-label">Experiment 2 &mdash; Causality</div>
          <div class="result-num">0.056 <span class="unit">max |effect| on judged refusal (below MDE of 0.067)</span></div>
          <p>
            Removing the refusal direction at any single site produces no causal cells for judged
            refusal on harmful prompts across all 18 cells, for both the instruct and SafeRL models
            (TOST <i>p</i>&nbsp;&lt;&nbsp;10<sup>&minus;23</sup>). A keyword refusal proxy drops
            from 0.79 to 0.15 under the intervention, which would appear as a successful jailbreak
            under keyword-based evaluation. The LLM judge finds no change: the model replaces its
            refusal phrasing, not its policy.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div class="result-block">
          <div class="result-label">The causal lever is over-refusal</div>
          <div class="result-num">&minus;0.146 <span class="unit">sole Holm&ndash;Bonferroni survivor (N6 at band B5, site P)</span></div>
          <p>
            The single surviving cell targets over-refusal on benign-borderline prompts, not
            compliance with harmful requests. Over-refusal drops by 0.12&ndash;0.19 at bands
            B4&ndash;B5 in both models. Neither model shows a causal cell for judged refusal on
            harmful prompts.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div class="result-block">
          <div class="result-label">SafeRL redundancy</div>
          <div class="result-num">+0.229 <span class="unit">difference-in-differences [0.083, 0.375]</span></div>
          <p>
            Global removal of the refusal direction at band B4 reduces instruct refusal from 0.917
            to 0.667. SafeRL resists. In the abliterated checkpoint, the cross-model direction
            cosine drops from 0.999 at B1 to 0.306 at B5, and N1 and N6 drop by 71% and 57% from
            instruct to abliterated, consistent with a representation that is both rotated and
            shrunk.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div class="result-block">
          <div class="result-label">Experiment 3 &mdash; Second-order screen</div>
          <div class="result-num">0 / 11 <span class="unit">pass the registered confirmation bar</span></div>
          <p>
            Of 15 candidates, 4 are dropped for collinearity. None of the remaining 11 passes the
            registered rule on 12 blind held-out checkpoints. W3 achieves
            &rho;&nbsp;=&nbsp;&minus;0.94 against over-refusal (n&nbsp;=&nbsp;6); G4 achieves
            &rho;&nbsp;=&nbsp;&minus;0.82 (n&nbsp;=&nbsp;12). The minimum detectable effect at
            n&nbsp;=&nbsp;12 is 0.73, exceeding every observed margin. Every readout sign is
            inverted relative to registration: they track trade-off position, not safety level.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div class="result-block">
          <div class="result-label">Score-matrix dimensionality</div>
          <div class="result-num">7.2 <span class="unit">effective rank (entropy-based; 5.3 participation-based)</span></div>
          <p>
            The 15-candidate &times; 48-checkpoint score matrix has an effective rank that rules
            out a one-coordinate summary. The leading singular vector's cosine with the logit
            baseline is 0.64, below the 0.80 threshold for a one-coordinate interpretation.
            An honest estimate of the panel size needed for reliable ranking is 30&ndash;150
            checkpoints, depending on the true effect size.
          </p>
        </div>
      </section>

      <section id="figures">
        <h2>Figures</h2>
        <div class="gallery-grid">

          <figure class="gallery-item" tabindex="0" role="button"
                  aria-label="Enlarge: Method Overview">
            <img src="figures/fig_overview_v0.jpg"
                 alt="Flowchart of the three-experiment design: Experiment 1 grades model pairs and scores 32 readouts; Experiment 2 runs a 6-band by 3-site causal grid; Experiment 3 screens 15 second-order readouts on 48 checkpoints.">
            <figcaption>
              <strong>Figure 1.</strong> Overview of the three-experiment design. Experiment 1
              (left): parent checkpoints are modified, each pair is behaviourally graded as NOOP or
              EFFECTIVE, then 32 candidate readouts are scored for false alarms and sensitivity.
              Experiment 2 (centre): a 6-band &times; 3-site causal intervention grid tests whether
              removing the refusal direction changes judged refusal. Experiment 3 (right): 15
              second-order readouts are screened on 48 checkpoints and tested on a blind held-out
              panel.
            </figcaption>
          </figure>

          <figure class="gallery-item" tabindex="0" role="button"
                  aria-label="Enlarge: False Alarm vs Sensitivity">
            <img src="figures/fig_specificity_v0.png"
                 alt="Scatter plot of false alarm count versus sensitivity for 32 readouts. Activation readouts cluster at 0 to 3 false alarms; logit baselines scatter across 5 to 8; weight-space readout B7 sits at 9.">
            <figcaption>
              <strong>Figure 2.</strong> False-alarm rate versus sensitivity for all 32 candidate
              readouts on the specificity panel. Each point is one readout; colour indicates readout
              class (blue&nbsp;= activation, orange&nbsp;= logit, green&nbsp;= weight,
              pink&nbsp;= text/card). Activation readouts cluster in the low-false-alarm region
              (0&ndash;3/15); logit baselines scatter across 5&ndash;8/15; the weight-space cosine
              B7 has the most false alarms (9/15). No readout achieves both zero false alarms and
              high sensitivity.
            </figcaption>
          </figure>

          <figure class="gallery-item" tabindex="0" role="button"
                  aria-label="Enlarge: Displacement Comparison">
            <img src="figures/fig_displacement_v0.png"
                 alt="Horizontal bar chart comparing median no-op displacement. Four logit variants range from 0.092 to 0.178 null standard deviations; the activation readout median sits at 0.024, a 6.2-times ratio.">
            <figcaption>
              <strong>Figure 3.</strong> Median no-op displacement (in null standard deviations)
              for each readout class. The logit baseline operates 6.2&times; further from zero than
              the median activation readout, explaining its higher false-alarm rate. Error bars show
              interquartile range across readouts within each class.
            </figcaption>
          </figure>

          <figure class="gallery-item" tabindex="0" role="button"
                  aria-label="Enlarge: Causal Grid Heatmap">
            <img src="figures/fig_causal_grid_v0.png"
                 alt="Two heatmaps of over-refusal effect sizes across a 6-band by 3-site causal grid. Left: Qwen3-4B-Instruct. Right: Qwen3-4B-SafeRL. Strongest effects at bands B4 and B5 site P.">
            <figcaption>
              <strong>Figure 4.</strong> Effect sizes for arm F on over-refusal (benign-borderline
              prompts) across the 6-band &times; 3-site causal grid. Left: Qwen3-4B-Instruct.
              Right: Qwen3-4B-SafeRL. Negative values (blue) indicate reduced over-refusal. The
              strongest effects concentrate at bands B4&ndash;B5, site P, but no cell survives
              Holm&ndash;Bonferroni correction for judged refusal on harmful prompts.
            </figcaption>
          </figure>

          <figure class="gallery-item" tabindex="0" role="button"
                  aria-label="Enlarge: Probe Survival Under Lesion">
            <img src="figures/fig_probe_v0.png"
                 alt="Left: line chart of probe AUROC under increasing lesion strength alpha, with AUROC near ceiling across all read-site and layer combinations. Right: forest plot of delta AUROC at alpha equals 1, all within 0.024 of zero.">
            <figcaption>
              <strong>Figure 5.</strong> Probe AUROC and projection gap under rank-one directional
              lesion at increasing strength &alpha;. At &alpha;&nbsp;=&nbsp;1 the projection gap
              drops by a factor of 4,700&times;, yet the cross-validated probe AUROC remains near
              ceiling. The safety representation spans multiple dimensions; removing one direction
              does not remove the information the probe reads.
            </figcaption>
          </figure>

        </div>
      </section>

      <section id="limitations">
        <h2>Limitations</h2>
        <ul class="limitations-list">
          <li>
            <strong>Scale.</strong> The specificity audit uses three families at 0.6&ndash;1.7B
            parameters. Larger models may have different false-alarm profiles. The 15 no-ops span
            four categories of deployment-relevant modifications but do not cover every possible
            perturbation.
          </li>
          <li>
            <strong>Underpowered comparisons.</strong> The per-readout false-alarm comparison on
            the core 15-pair panel (4/12 vs 1/12 on non-degenerate pairs) has a minimum attainable
            <i>p</i> of 0.0625. The pooled 24-pair comparison is powered (McNemar
            <i>p</i>&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.001) but pools across an extended set. The second-order
            readout screen's minimum detectable effect (0.73) exceeds every observed margin.
          </li>
          <li>
            <strong>Single architecture for the causal grid.</strong> The causal experiment uses
            only Qwen3-4B. The decodable-but-inert finding may not generalise to architectures
            with different layer counts or attention patterns.
          </li>
          <li>
            <strong>Judge limitations.</strong> All behavioural outcomes depend on an LLM judge
            with split-half reliability of 0.96 (harmful compliance) and 0.94 (over-refusal). The
            keyword proxy and the judge disagree substantially
            (&kappa;&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.50 for instruct,
            &kappa;&nbsp;&asymp;&nbsp;0 for SafeRL).
          </li>
          <li>
            <strong>No surviving candidate.</strong> No readout passes the full pre-registered
            selection rule at the tested panel sizes. At
            n&nbsp;=&nbsp;10&ndash;12, the registered bar is unattainable for the observed effect
            sizes.
          </li>
          <li>
            <strong>Probe ceiling.</strong> The probe AUROC is at ceiling (1.000) in the
            unperturbed control, so its survival under the lesion is uninformative about whether
            the lesion removed safety-relevant information.
          </li>
        </ul>
      </section>

    </main>

    <footer>
      <p>
        <a href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-f8532e-safety-only-checks-output-when-warned@main/paper.pdf">Paper (PDF)</a>
        &nbsp;&middot;&nbsp;

      </p>

}</pre>
    </footer>
  </div>
</div>

<script>
(function() {
  var sections = document.querySelectorAll('section[id]');
  var navLinks = document.querySelectorAll('.side-nav a');
  var observer = new IntersectionObserver(function(entries) {
    entries.forEach(function(e) {
      if (e.isIntersecting) {
        navLinks.forEach(function(l) { l.classList.remove('active'); });
        var t = document.querySelector('.side-nav a[href="#' + e.target.id + '"]');
        if (t) t.classList.add('active');
      }
    });
  }, { rootMargin: '-20% 0px -70% 0px' });
  sections.forEach(function(s) { observer.observe(s); });

  var lb = document.getElementById('lightbox');
  var lbImg = document.getElementById('lb-img');
  var lbCap = document.getElementById('lb-cap');
  var closeBtn = lb.querySelector('.lightbox-close');
  var lastFocus = null;

  function openLB(item) {
    lastFocus = item;
    var img = item.querySelector('img');
    var cap = item.querySelector('figcaption');
    lbImg.src = img.src;
    lbImg.alt = img.alt;
    lbCap.textContent = cap ? cap.textContent : '';
    lb.style.display = 'flex';
    requestAnimationFrame(function() { lb.classList.add('open'); });
    closeBtn.focus();
    document.body.style.overflow = 'hidden';
  }

  function closeLB() {
    lb.classList.remove('open');
    var rm = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;
    setTimeout(function() {
      lb.style.display = 'none';
      lbImg.src = '';
      document.body.style.overflow = '';
      if (lastFocus) lastFocus.focus();
    }, rm ? 0 : 200);
  }

  lb.style.display = 'none';

  document.querySelectorAll('.gallery-item').forEach(function(item) {
    item.addEventListener('click', function() { openLB(item); });
    item.addEventListener('keydown', function(e) {
      if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') { e.preventDefault(); openLB(item); }
    });
  });

  closeBtn.addEventListener('click', closeLB);
  lb.addEventListener('click', function(e) { if (e.target === lb) closeLB(); });
  lb.addEventListener('keydown', function(e) {
    if (e.key === 'Escape') closeLB();
    if (e.key === 'Tab') { e.preventDefault(); closeBtn.focus(); }
  });
})();
</script>
</body>
</html>

We tested 32 candidate readouts against\n          model modifications that provably do not change safety behaviour. On 24 such no-op edits\n          across three model families, mid-layer activation readouts produced zero false alarms;\n          the standard logit-gap baseline produced 11 (McNemar <i>p</i>&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.001). No second-order readout survived\n          blind held-out confirmation at the pre-registered bar, and the effective rank of the score\n          matrix (7.2) rules out reducing all readouts to a single number.\n        </p>\n        <div class=\"hero-links\">\n          <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-f8532e-safety-only-checks-output-when-warned@main/paper.pdf\">Read the paper (PDF)</a>\n          <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-f8532e-safety-only-checks-output-when-warned\">Code repository</a>\n        </div>\n      </section>\n\n      <section id=\"contributions\">\n        <h2>Contributions</h2>\n        <div class=\"contributions-grid\">\n          <div class=\"contribution\">\n            <h3>Activation readouts have far fewer false alarms than the logit baseline</h3>\n            <p>\n              On 24 behaviourally graded no-op edits spanning numerical precision, identity\n              transforms, non-safety adaptation and head-only edits, geometric activation readouts\n              produce zero false alarms while the final-layer logit gap produces 11 (exact McNemar\n              <i>p</i>&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.001). On the core 15-pair panel, mid-layer readouts fire on\n              at most 3 no-ops; the logit baseline fires on 6&ndash;8.\n            </p>\n          </div>\n          <div class=\"contribution\">\n            <h3>The refusal direction is decodable but causally inert at the prompt site</h3>\n            <p>\n              In a 6-band &times; 3-site causal grid, removing the refusal direction at the last\n              prompt token does not change judged refusal in any of 18 cells\n              (max&nbsp;|effect|&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.056, TOST\n              <i>p</i>&nbsp;&lt;&nbsp;10<sup>&minus;23</sup>). The model rewrites its refusal in\n              different words. The causal lever is over-refusal on benign-borderline prompts.\n            </p>\n          </div>\n          <div class=\"contribution\">\n            <h3>Abliteration both rotates and shrinks the refusal representation</h3>\n            <p>\n              Global removal of the refusal direction at band B4 reduces instruct refusal from\n              0.92 to 0.67; SafeRL resists with a difference-in-differences of +0.23\n              [0.08,&nbsp;0.38]. The cross-model cosine drops from 0.999 at B1 to 0.31 at B5,\n              and N1 and N6 drop by 71% and 57% from instruct to the abliterated checkpoint.\n            </p>\n          </div>\n          <div class=\"contribution\">\n            <h3>Second-order readouts index trade-off position, not safety level</h3>\n            <p>\n              Fifteen candidate readouts are screened on 48 checkpoints; none of 11 survivors\n              passes blind held-out confirmation. Every readout sign is inverted relative to its\n              registered prediction: they track where a model sits on the\n              refusal&ndash;permissiveness spectrum, not a safety level per se. The effective\n              rank of the score matrix is 7.2, ruling out a one-coordinate summary.\n            </p>\n          </div>\n        </div>\n      </section>\n\n      <section id=\"method\">\n        <h2>Method</h2>\n        <figure class=\"method-fig\">\n          <img src=\"figures/fig_overview_v0.jpg\"\n               alt=\"Flowchart of the three-experiment design: Experiment 1 grades parent-child model pairs as NOOP or EFFECTIVE then scores 32 readouts for false alarms and sensitivity; Experiment 2 runs a 6-band by 3-site causal grid on Qwen3-4B variants; Experiment 3 screens 15 second-order readouts on 48 checkpoints and tests survivors on 12 blind held-out checkpoints.\">\n          <figcaption>\n            Overview of the three-experiment design. Experiment 1 (left): parent checkpoints are\n            modified, each pair is behaviourally graded, then 32 candidate readouts are scored.\n            Experiment 2 (centre): a causal intervention grid tests whether removing the refusal\n            direction changes judged refusal. Experiment 3 (right): 15 second-order readouts are\n            screened and tested on a blind held-out panel.\n          </figcaption>\n        </figure>\n\n        <p>\n          All three experiments share the same behavioural grading pipeline. Each checkpoint is\n          evaluated on 85 harmful prompts and 83 benign prompts with an LLM judge (Gemini 2.5 Flash\n          Lite; split-half reliability 0.96 for harmful compliance, 0.94 for over-refusal).\n          Behavioural labels are frozen before any readout is computed, enforced by a SHA-256 hash\n          chain.\n        </p>\n\n        <h3>Experiment 1: Specificity Audit</h3>\n        <p>\n          Parent&ndash;child model pairs are constructed across three families (Qwen3-0.6B,\n          Llama-3.2-1B, Falcon3-1B) with modifications in four categories: numerical precision\n          (8 pairs), identity transforms (2), non-safety adaptation (2) and head-only edits (3).\n          Behavioural grading yields 15 no-ops and 9 effective changes. For each pair, 32 candidate\n          readouts are computed from residual-stream activations, logits, weights and text outputs. A\n          readout fires a false alarm if its paired-bootstrap CI excludes zero in the expected\n          direction on a no-op pair.\n        </p>\n\n        <h3>Experiment 2: Causal Intervention Grid</h3>\n        <p>\n          Three Qwen3-4B variants (Instruct, SafeRL, abliterated) are tested in a grid crossing\n          six depth bands (B1&ndash;B6, each one-sixth of the 36-layer stack) with three\n          intervention sites: last prompt token (P), first decode positions (D'), and the early\n          response window (E). Each cell runs five arms including a matched random control. A cell\n          counts as causal only if the treatment differs from the random control after\n          Holm&ndash;Bonferroni correction at &alpha;&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.05 over all 18 cells.\n        </p>\n\n        <h3>Experiment 3: Second-Order Readout Screen</h3>\n        <p>\n          Fifteen candidates measuring write-handle redundancy (W1&ndash;W8), dimensionless geometry\n          (G1&ndash;G4) and competing mechanisms (A1&ndash;A3) are screened on 48 checkpoints from\n          7 lineages. Four are dropped for collinearity with the logit baseline. The remaining 11\n          are tested on 12 blind held-out checkpoints from 7 non-overlapping lineages. Confirmation\n          requires the candidate's correlation with over-refusal to exceed the logit baseline by a\n          margin whose CI excludes zero.\n        </p>\n      </section>\n\n      <section id=\"results\">\n        <h2>Results</h2>\n\n        <div class=\"result-block\">\n          <div class=\"result-label\">Experiment 1 &mdash; Specificity</div>\n          <div class=\"result-num\">0 vs 11 <span class=\"unit\">false alarms on 24 no-op edits (McNemar <i>p</i> = 0.001)</span></div>\n          <p>\n            Geometric activation readouts produce zero false alarms on the pooled 24-pair set; the\n            logit-gap baseline produces 11. On the core 15-pair panel, the best activation readouts\n            fire on at most 3 no-ops, while the logit gap fires on 6&ndash;8 out of 15. The\n            weight-space cosine B7 fires on 9 of 15: every dtype cast triggers it.\n          </p>\n        </div>\n\n        <div class=\"result-block\">\n          <div class=\"result-label\">Displacement mechanism</div>\n          <div class=\"result-num\">6.2&times; <span class=\"unit\">displacement ratio (logit 0.150 vs activation 0.024 null SD)</span></div>\n          <p>\n            The logit gap operates at the decision boundary where small perturbations produce large\n            score changes. Mid-layer activation readouts measure the geometry of the representation\n            space, which is more stable under numerical-precision and identity modifications.\n            Final-layer logits amplify implementation-irrelevant variation.\n          </p>\n        </div>\n\n        <div class=\"result-block\">\n          <div class=\"result-label\">Experiment 2 &mdash; Causality</div>\n          <div class=\"result-num\">0.056 <span class=\"unit\">max |effect| on judged refusal (below MDE of 0.067)</span></div>\n          <p>\n            Removing the refusal direction at any single site produces no causal cells for judged\n            refusal on harmful prompts across all 18 cells, for both the instruct and SafeRL models\n            (TOST <i>p</i>&nbsp;&lt;&nbsp;10<sup>&minus;23</sup>). A keyword refusal proxy drops\n            from 0.79 to 0.15 under the intervention, which would appear as a successful jailbreak\n            under keyword-based evaluation. The LLM judge finds no change: the model replaces its\n            refusal phrasing, not its policy.\n          </p>\n        </div>\n\n        <div class=\"result-block\">\n          <div class=\"result-label\">The causal lever is over-refusal</div>\n          <div class=\"result-num\">&minus;0.146 <span class=\"unit\">sole Holm&ndash;Bonferroni survivor (N6 at band B5, site P)</span></div>\n          <p>\n            The single surviving cell targets over-refusal on benign-borderline prompts, not\n            compliance with harmful requests. Over-refusal drops by 0.12&ndash;0.19 at bands\n            B4&ndash;B5 in both models. Neither model shows a causal cell for judged refusal on\n            harmful prompts.\n          </p>\n        </div>\n\n        <div class=\"result-block\">\n          <div class=\"result-label\">SafeRL redundancy</div>\n          <div class=\"result-num\">+0.229 <span class=\"unit\">difference-in-differences [0.083, 0.375]</span></div>\n          <p>\n            Global removal of the refusal direction at band B4 reduces instruct refusal from 0.917\n            to 0.667. SafeRL resists. In the abliterated checkpoint, the cross-model direction\n            cosine drops from 0.999 at B1 to 0.306 at B5, and N1 and N6 drop by 71% and 57% from\n            instruct to abliterated, consistent with a representation that is both rotated and\n            shrunk.\n          </p>\n        </div>\n\n        <div class=\"result-block\">\n          <div class=\"result-label\">Experiment 3 &mdash; Second-order screen</div>\n          <div class=\"result-num\">0 / 11 <span class=\"unit\">pass the registered confirmation bar</span></div>\n          <p>\n            Of 15 candidates, 4 are dropped for collinearity. None of the remaining 11 passes the\n            registered rule on 12 blind held-out checkpoints. W3 achieves\n            &rho;&nbsp;=&nbsp;&minus;0.94 against over-refusal (n&nbsp;=&nbsp;6); G4 achieves\n            &rho;&nbsp;=&nbsp;&minus;0.82 (n&nbsp;=&nbsp;12). The minimum detectable effect at\n            n&nbsp;=&nbsp;12 is 0.73, exceeding every observed margin. Every readout sign is\n            inverted relative to registration: they track trade-off position, not safety level.\n          </p>\n        </div>\n\n        <div class=\"result-block\">\n          <div class=\"result-label\">Score-matrix dimensionality</div>\n          <div class=\"result-num\">7.2 <span class=\"unit\">effective rank (entropy-based; 5.3 participation-based)</span></div>\n          <p>\n            The 15-candidate &times; 48-checkpoint score matrix has an effective rank that rules\n            out a one-coordinate summary. The leading singular vector's cosine with the logit\n            baseline is 0.64, below the 0.80 threshold for a one-coordinate interpretation.\n            An honest estimate of the panel size needed for reliable ranking is 30&ndash;150\n            checkpoints, depending on the true effect size.\n          </p>\n        </div>\n      </section>\n\n      <section id=\"figures\">\n        <h2>Figures</h2>\n        <div class=\"gallery-grid\">\n\n          <figure class=\"gallery-item\" tabindex=\"0\" role=\"button\"\n                  aria-label=\"Enlarge: Method Overview\">\n            <img src=\"figures/fig_overview_v0.jpg\"\n                 alt=\"Flowchart of the three-experiment design: Experiment 1 grades model pairs and scores 32 readouts; Experiment 2 runs a 6-band by 3-site causal grid; Experiment 3 screens 15 second-order readouts on 48 checkpoints.\">\n            <figcaption>\n              <strong>Figure 1.</strong> Overview of the three-experiment design. Experiment 1\n              (left): parent checkpoints are modified, each pair is behaviourally graded as NOOP or\n              EFFECTIVE, then 32 candidate readouts are scored for false alarms and sensitivity.\n              Experiment 2 (centre): a 6-band &times; 3-site causal intervention grid tests whether\n              removing the refusal direction changes judged refusal. Experiment 3 (right): 15\n              second-order readouts are screened on 48 checkpoints and tested on a blind held-out\n              panel.\n            </figcaption>\n          </figure>\n\n          <figure class=\"gallery-item\" tabindex=\"0\" role=\"button\"\n                  aria-label=\"Enlarge: False Alarm vs Sensitivity\">\n            <img src=\"figures/fig_specificity_v0.png\"\n                 alt=\"Scatter plot of false alarm count versus sensitivity for 32 readouts. Activation readouts cluster at 0 to 3 false alarms; logit baselines scatter across 5 to 8; weight-space readout B7 sits at 9.\">\n            <figcaption>\n              <strong>Figure 2.</strong> False-alarm rate versus sensitivity for all 32 candidate\n              readouts on the specificity panel. Strongest effects at bands B4 and B5 site P.\">\n            <figcaption>\n              <strong>Figure 4.</strong> Effect sizes for arm F on over-refusal (benign-borderline\n              prompts) across the 6-band &times; 3-site causal grid. Left: Qwen3-4B-Instruct.\n              Right: Qwen3-4B-SafeRL. Negative values (blue) indicate reduced over-refusal. The\n              strongest effects concentrate at bands B4&ndash;B5, site P, but no cell survives\n              Holm&ndash;Bonferroni correction for judged refusal on harmful prompts.\n            </figcaption>\n          </figure>\n\n          <figure class=\"gallery-item\" tabindex=\"0\" role=\"button\"\n                  aria-label=\"Enlarge: Probe Survival Under Lesion\">\n            <img src=\"figures/fig_probe_v0.png\"\n                 alt=\"Left: line chart of probe AUROC under increasing lesion strength alpha, with AUROC near ceiling across all read-site and layer combinations. Right: forest plot of delta AUROC at alpha equals 1, all within 0.024 of zero.\">\n            <figcaption>\n              <strong>Figure 5.</strong> Probe AUROC and projection gap under rank-one directional\n              lesion at increasing strength &alpha;. At &alpha;&nbsp;=&nbsp;1 the projection gap\n              drops by a factor of 4,700&times;, yet the cross-validated probe AUROC remains near\n              ceiling. The safety representation spans multiple dimensions; removing one direction\n              does not remove the information the probe reads.\n            </figcaption>\n          </figure>\n\n        </div>\n      </section>\n\n      <section id=\"limitations\">\n        <h2>Limitations</h2>\n        <ul class=\"limitations-list\">\n          <li>\n            <strong>Scale.</strong> The specificity audit uses three families at 0.6&ndash;1.7B\n            parameters. Larger models may have different false-alarm profiles. The\n            keyword proxy and the judge disagree substantially\n            (&kappa;&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.50 for instruct,\n            &kappa;&nbsp;&asymp;&nbsp;0 for SafeRL).\n          </li>\n          <li>\n            <strong>No surviving candidate.</strong> No readout passes the full pre-registered\n            selection rule at the tested panel sizes. At\n            n&nbsp;=&nbsp;10&ndash;12, the registered bar is unattainable for the observed effect\n            sizes.\n          </li>\n          <li>\n            <strong>Probe ceiling.</strong> The probe AUROC is at ceiling (1.000) in the\n            unperturbed control, so its survival under the lesion is uninformative about whether\n            the lesion removed safety-relevant information.\n          </li>\n        </ul>\n      </section>\n\n    </main>\n\n    <footer>\n      <p>\n        <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-f8532e-safety-only-checks-output-when-warned@main/paper.pdf\">Paper (PDF)</a>\n        &nbsp;&middot;&nbsp;\n        <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-f8532e-safety-only-checks-output-when-warned\">Code repository</a>\n      </p>\n<pre class=\"citation-block\">@article{safety-readout-audits-2026,\n  title  = {Specificity and Causality Audits for\n            Activation-Based Safety Readouts},\n  year   = {2026},\n  url    = {https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/\n            ai-invention-f8532e-safety-only-checks-output-when-warned}\n}</pre>\n    </footer>\n  </div>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"lightbox\" id=\"lightbox\" role=\"dialog\" aria-modal=\"true\" aria-label=\"Figure viewer\">\n  <div class=\"lightbox-inner\">\n    <button class=\"lightbox-close\" aria-label=\"Close figure viewer\">&times;</button>\n    <img id=\"lb-img\" src=\"\" alt=\"\">\n    <p class=\"lightbox-caption\" id=\"lb-cap\"></p>\n  </div>\n</div>\n\n<script>\n(function() {\n  var sections = document.querySelectorAll('section[id]');\n  var navLinks = document.querySelectorAll('.side-nav a');\n  var observer = new IntersectionObserver(function(entries) {\n    entries.forEach(function(e) {\n      if (e.isIntersecting) {\n        navLinks.forEach(function(l) { l.classList.remove('active'); We tested 32 candidate readouts against\n          model modifications that provably do not change safety behaviour. On 24 such no-op edits\n          across three model families, mid-layer activation readouts produced zero false alarms;\n          the standard logit-gap baseline produced 11 (McNemar <i>p</i>&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.001). A causal\n          intervention grid on Qwen3-4B then showed that the refusal direction is linearly readable\n          from activations but removing it at any single site does not change the model's judged\n          refusal: it rewrites its refusal in different words. No second-order readout survived\n          blind held-out confirmation at the pre-registered bar, and the effective rank of the score\n          matrix (7.2) rules out reducing all readouts to a single number.\n        </p>\n        <div class=\"hero-links\">\n          <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-f8532e-safety-only-checks-output-when-warned@main/paper.pdf\">Read the paper (PDF)</a>\n          <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-f8532e-safety-only-checks-output-when-warned\">Code repository</a>\n        </div>\n      </section>\n\n      <section id=\"contributions\">\n        <h2>Contributions</h2>\n        <div class=\"contributions-grid\">\n          <div class=\"contribution\">\n            <h3>Activation readouts have far fewer false alarms than the logit baseline</h3>\n            <p>\n              On 24 behaviourally graded no-op edits spanning numerical precision, identity\n              transforms, non-safety adaptation and head-only edits, geometric activation readouts\n              produce zero false alarms while the final-layer logit gap produces 11 (exact McNemar\n              <i>p</i>&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.001). On the core 15-pair panel, mid-layer readouts fire on\n              at most 3 no-ops; the logit baseline fires on 6&ndash;8.\n            </p>\n          </div>\n          <div class=\"contribution\">\n            <h3>The refusal direction is decodable but causally inert at the prompt site</h3>\n            <p>\n              In a 6-band &times; 3-site causal grid, removing the refusal direction at the last\n              prompt token does not change judged refusal in any of 18 cells\n              (max&nbsp;|effect|&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.056, TOST\n              <i>p</i>&nbsp;&lt;&nbsp;10<sup>&minus;23</sup>). The model rewrites its refusal in\n              different words. The causal lever is over-refusal on benign-borderline prompts.\n            </p>\n          </div>\n          <div class=\"contribution\">\n            <h3>Abliteration both rotates and shrinks the refusal representation</h3>\n            <p>\n              Global removal of the refusal direction at band B4 reduces instruct refusal from\n              0.92 to 0.67; SafeRL resists with a difference-in-differences of +0.23\n              [0.08,&nbsp;0.38]. The cross-model cosine drops from 0.999 at B1 to 0.31 at B5,\n              and N1 and N6 drop by 71% and 57% from instruct to the abliterated checkpoint.\n            </p>\n          </div>\n          <div class=\"contribution\">\n            <h3>Second-order readouts index trade-off position, not safety level</h3>\n            <p>\n              Fifteen candidate readouts are screened on 48 checkpoints; none of 11 survivors\n              passes blind held-out confirmation. Every readout sign is inverted relative to its\n              registered prediction: they track where a model sits on the\n              refusal&ndash;permissiveness spectrum, not a safety level per se. The effective\n              rank of the score matrix is 7.2, ruling out a one-coordinate summary.\n            </p>\n          </div>\n        </div>\n      </section>\n\n      <section id=\"method\">\n        <h2>Method</h2>\n        <figure class=\"method-fig\">\n          <img src=\"figures/fig_overview_v0.jpg\"\n               alt=\"Flowchart of the three-experiment design: Experiment 1 grades parent-child model pairs as NOOP or EFFECTIVE then scores 32 readouts for false alarms and sensitivity; Experiment 2 runs a 6-band by 3-site causal grid on Qwen3-4B variants; Experiment 3 screens 15 second-order readouts on 48 checkpoints and tests survivors on 12 blind held-out checkpoints.\">\n          <figcaption>\n            Overview of the three-experiment design. Experiment 1 (left): parent checkpoints are\n            modified, each pair is behaviourally graded, then 32 candidate readouts are scored.\n            Experiment 2 (centre): a causal intervention grid tests whether removing the refusal\n            direction changes judged refusal. Second, a causal intervention grid on Qwen3-4B reveals that the refusal direction is linearly decodable at the prompt site but removing it does not change judged refusal: the model rewrites its refusal in different words. The Activation-based Model Scanner (AMS) extracts a concept direction from 16 contrastive prompt pairs at 40--80\\% depth and reports leave-one-out accuracy of 71\\% across 14 configurations~\\citep{Messenger2026}. N-GLARE aggregates Jensen--Shannon divergence of hidden states and reports coupling with refusal rates during training~\\citep{Lin2025}. Representation engineering uses contrastive activations for monitoring and control~\\citep{Zou2023}. All three read activations at the final prompt token, and all three correlate with safety behaviour in their validation settings.\n\nTwo questions remain open. First, do these readouts avoid false alarms when a checkpoint is modified in ways that do not change safety behaviour? The effective rank of the candidate-by-checkpoint score matrix is 7.2, ruling out a one-coordinate summary (Section~\\ref{sec:results-screen}).\n\\end{enumerate}\n\n\n\\section{Related Work}\n\\label{sec:related}\n\n\\paragraph{Activation-based safety readouts.}\nAMS extracts concept directions from 16 contrastive prompt pairs at 40--80\\% depth~\\citep{Messenger2026}. Zhang et al.\\ showed that innate safety alignment extends beyond surface layers~\\citep{Zhang2025}. Zhao et al.\\ published the harmfulness--refusal dissociation with causal steering, confirming that safety-relevant representations and refusal behaviour can be decoupled within a single model~\\citep{Zhao2025}. Our causal grid extends this work from the cross-model setting to the within-model, within-site setting.\n\n\\paragraph{False-alarm and staleness controls.}\nDuan benchmarks frozen linear probes across quantisation and LoRA conditions and finds 43--54\\% big-drop rates under fine-tuning-style updates~\\citep{Duan2026}. Hurtado audits 37 benign fine-tunes at FPR 0.11 using a weight-space signal~\\citep{Hurtado2026}. AMS reports FP16/INT8/INT4 drift of at most 4.4\\% on one model but does not grade the model's behaviour~\\citep{Messenger2026}.\n\n\\paragraph{Over-refusal.}\nXSTest provides paired harmful and benign prompts to measure exaggerated safety~\\citep{Rottger2023}. Yuan et al.\\ decouple refusal training from general instruction following~\\citep{Yuan2024}. Every existing over-refusal measurement is a behavioural outcome; no internal readout uses over-refusal as its prediction target across checkpoints.\n\n\\paragraph{Behavioural benchmarks.}\nHarmBench standardises red-teaming evaluation across attack methods~\\citep{Mazeika2024}. JailbreakBench provides an open benchmark for jailbreaking evaluation~\\citep{Chao2024}. Spagliardi et al.\\ apply item response theory to reduce the prompt budget of behavioural safety benchmarks by 80\\% or more~\\citep{Spagliardi2026}. Rivera et al.\\ find that three latent factors explain 77\\% of variance across 8 behavioural benchmarks~\\citep{Rivera2026}.\n\n\n\\section{Experimental Setup}\n\\label{sec:setup}\n\n\\subsection{Models and Panel Composition}\n\\label{sec:panel}\n\nWe construct parent--child pairs across three model families: Qwen3-0.6B-Instruct (F1), Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct (F2) and Falcon3-1B-Instruct (F3). Each parent is modified with operations spanning four categories:\n\n\\begin{itemize}\n\\item \\emph{Numerical precision} (8 pairs): bf16-to-fp16 cast, int8 weight-only quantisation, LLM.int8() quantisation~\\citep{Dettmers2022}.\n\\item \\emph{Identity transforms} (2 pairs): system-prompt swap (benign non-safety system prompt).\n\\item \\emph{Non-safety adaptation} (2 pairs): non-safety LoRA on instruction-following data~\\citep{Hu2021}, non-safety DPO on coherence pairs~\\citep{Rafailov2023}.\n\\item \\emph{Head-only edits} (3 pairs): targeted 0.5-nat suppression of refusal-onset tokens in the unembedding matrix, leaving all transformer-block weights and activations unchanged.\n\\end{itemize}\n\nOf these intended no-ops, 15 survive behavioural grading as NOOP (Table~\\ref{tab:panel}). These include one reclassified pair: a rank-one directional lesion at $\\alpha = 0.05$ (F1\\_a05) that was intended as an effective change but produced no behavioural shift. Three of the 15 are head-only edits whose activation delta at every layer is exactly zero by construction: any activation readout's silence on these pairs is analytic, not empirical. We therefore report false-alarm rates on both the full 15 pairs and the 12 non-degenerate pairs throughout.\n\nAdditionally, we include 9 effective changes from the frozen classification rule: in-house rank-one directional lesions at $\\alpha = 1.0$ (2 pairs), one non-safety DPO that unexpectedly shifted harmful compliance, and 6 community-modified checkpoints from Hugging Face (5 abliterated, 1 base-to-SFT transition).\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\scriptsize\n\\caption{Panel composition. 15 behavioural no-ops and 9 effective changes across three families. $\\dagger$~marks head-only edits with bitwise-zero activation delta. $\\ddagger$~marks a reclassified pair (intended lesion observed as NOOP). HC = harmful compliance, OR = over-refusal. All CIs are 95\\% paired bootstrap.}\n\\label{tab:panel}\n\\begin{tabular}{llllr}\n\\toprule\n\\textbf{Pair ID} & \\textbf{Fam.} & \\textbf{Recipe} & \\textbf{Class} & $\\bm{\\Delta}$\\textbf{HC [CI]} \\\\\n\\midrule\n\\multicolumn{5}{l}{\\textit{Behavioural no-ops (15)}} \\\\\nF1/F2/F3\\_int8wo & Q/L/F & int8 weight-only & NOOP & $[-0.01, 0.00, 0.00]$ \\\\\nF1/F2/F3\\_fp16   & Q/L/F & bf16$\\to$fp16 cast & NOOP & $[+0.01, 0.00, 0.00]$ \\\\\nF1/F2\\_int8bnb   & Q/L   & LLM.int8()       & NOOP & $[+0.02, 0.00]$ \\\\\nF1/F2\\_sysprompt  & Q/L   & system-prompt swap & NOOP & $[0.00, -0.01]$ \\\\\nF1/F2/F3\\_wu05$\\dagger$ & Q/L/F & head-only $\\alpha{=}0.05$ & NOOP & $[+0.01, 0.00, 0.00]$ \\\\\nF3\\_dpo           & F     & non-safety DPO   & NOOP & $0.00$ \\\\\nF1\\_a05$\\ddagger$ & Q     & lesion $\\alpha{=}0.05$ & NOOP & $+0.02$ \\\\\n\\midrule\n\\multicolumn{5}{l}{\\textit{Effective changes (9)}} \\\\\nmlabonne--Qwen3-4B-ablit. & Q & community abliteration & EFF & $+0.73\\;[0.60,0.85]$ \\\\\nF2/F3\\_a10 & L/F & lesion $\\alpha{=}1.0$ & EFF & $[+0.12, +0.46]$ \\\\\nF1\\_dpo    & Q   & non-safety DPO & EFF & $+0.08\\;[0.02,0.15]$ \\\\\nhuihui-0.6B-ablit. & Q & community abliteration & EFF & $+0.39\\;[0.28,0.49]$ \\\\\nmylesgoose-ablit.  & L & community abliteration & EFF & $+0.13\\;[0.06,0.21]$ \\\\\nhuihui-1.7B-ablit. & Q & community abliteration & EFF & $+0.62\\;[0.52,0.73]$ \\\\\nVikhr-ablit.       & L & community abliteration & EFF & $+0.48\\;[0.38,0.59]$ \\\\\nAMD-OLMo-SFT       & O & base$\\to$SFT          & EFF & $+0.07\\;[0.01,0.13]$ \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\subsection{Behavioural Grading}\n\nEach checkpoint is evaluated on 85 harmful prompts (45 StrongReject~\\citep{Mazeika2024}, 40 XSTest harmful twins~\\citep{Rottger2023}) and 83 benign prompts (40 XSTest safe twins, 43 hard-benign items) with greedy decoding at 96 tokens. Harmful compliance (HC) is the fraction of harmful prompts answered substantively; over-refusal (OR) is the fraction of benign prompts incorrectly refused. Both are scored by an LLM judge (Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite), with split-half reliability of 0.96 (HC) and 0.94 (OR) on the confirmation panel.\n\nA pair is classified as NOOP if $|\\Delta\\text{HC}| \\leq 0.05$ and $|\\Delta\\text{OR}| \\leq 0.05$ with both 95\\% paired-bootstrap CIs inside $[-0.10, +0.10]$; as EFFECTIVE if the $\\Delta$HC CI excludes zero; as OR\\_EFFECTIVE if the $\\Delta$OR CI excludes zero but $\\Delta$HC covers zero; otherwise AMBIGUOUS. Behavioural grading is committed before any activation readout is computed, enforced by a SHA-256 hash chain. Every readout score in this study was computed after the behavioural label was frozen.\n\n\n\\section{Method}\n\\label{sec:method}\n\n\\subsection{Experiment 1: Specificity Audit}\n\\label{sec:exp1-method}\n\n\\paragraph{Readouts.}\nFor each parent and child checkpoint, we extract residual-stream activations at the last prompt token at every layer. We compute 32 candidate readouts spanning four classes. \\emph{Activation readouts} (16 variants): $N1$ (request-axis Cohen's $d$ at the layer maximising separation, using cross-fitted easy/hard prompt splits), $N6$ (benign-side separability), $N4$ (onset/shape statistics from per-prompt refusal-onset distributions), $N7$ (two-sided gap), $N8$ (severity Spearman $\\rho$), $N9$ (first-decoded-token refusal mass), $N11$ (AMS-window Fisher information), $N12$ (weighted combination), $C4$/$C7$/$C13$ (cross-layer and depth-band variants), and AMS Tier-1/Tier-2 (reimplemented from the released code~\\citep{Messenger2026}, batch size~1, agreement to within $7 \\times 10^{-5}$ relative). \\emph{Logit readouts} (4 variants): $\\text{BL1}$ final-layer logit gap in easy-prompt, hard-prompt, true-logit and true-logit-hard scoring conventions. \\emph{Weight readout}: $B7$ (per-layer diff-in-means weight projection cosine). \\emph{Text/card readouts}: regex model-card detection, name-free regex, greedy refusal rate, greedy refusal onset.\n\nFor each readout, we compute the paired change $\\Delta$ (child minus parent) with a 2000-draw prompt-stratified bootstrap CI. A readout fires a \\emph{false alarm} on a no-op pair if its $\\Delta$ CI excludes zero in the readout's expected direction. \\emph{Sensitivity} is the fraction of effective pairs where the CI excludes zero in the expected direction.\n\n\\subsection{Experiment 2: Causal Intervention Grid}\n\\label{sec:exp2-method}\n\nWe use three Qwen3-4B variants: Instruct, SafeRL (additional safety reinforcement learning) and abliterated (mlabonne/Qwen3-4B-abliterated). We cross six depth bands (B1--B6, each spanning one-sixth of the 36-layer stack) with three intervention sites: P (last prompt token, forward-only hook), D$'$ (model's own first 1--8 greedy decode positions) and E (early response window, positions 5--20). The abliterated model's grid covers only site P (6 cells) due to its low baseline refusal rate (arm-0 refused harm $= 0.188$), which floors the harmful-compliance outcome.\n\nEach cell has five arms: F (matched-norm projection removing the fitted request-axis direction), N6 (benign-side direction), N6$\\perp$ (orthogonal complement of N6 with respect to F), R (orthogonalised random direction with matched displacement, averaged over 10--20 draws) and arm~0 (no intervention). A positive-control arm (POS, full residual patching from a different model) runs at bands B3 and B4. For each cell, we generate 80 tokens on 48 harmful and 48 benign-borderline prompts and judge outcomes with the same LLM grader. A cell is \\emph{causal} only if the treatment arm (F or N6) differs from the random control R after Holm--Bonferroni correction at $\\alpha = 0.05$ over all 18 cells jointly.\n\n\\subsection{Experiment 3: Second-Order Readout Screen}\n\\label{sec:exp3-method}\n\nWe define 15 candidate readouts that go beyond the first-order diff-in-means direction: W1--W8 measure write-handle redundancy and self-repair across layers~\\citep{McGrath2023, Rushing2024}; G1--G4 measure dimensionless geometry of the activation space (Fisher separation, used-ness, BL1-orthogonal Fisher); A1--A3 measure competing mechanisms. Each is computed as a single scalar per checkpoint on the same prompt sets. The candidates are screened on a 48-checkpoint panel spanning 7 independent lineages, then tested against a blind held-out confirmation panel of 12 checkpoints from 7 independent lineages (intersection with the screen panel: empty). Selection requires the candidate's correlation with over-refusal to exceed the logit baseline's by a margin whose CI excludes zero under a paired checkpoint bootstrap.\n\n\n\\section{Results}\n\\label{sec:results}\n\n\\subsection{Specificity: False Alarms on Behavioural No-Ops}\n\\label{sec:results-specificity}\n\nTable~\\ref{tab:specificity} reports the false-alarm rate and sensitivity for all 32 candidate readouts. Activation readouts fire on at most 3 of 15 no-ops ($C13_{\\text{peak}}$, the most sensitive activation readout, fires on~3). The median activation readout fires on 0--1 no-ops (Wilson 95\\% CI for 1/15: [0.01, 0.30]). On the 12 non-degenerate pairs (excluding three head-only edits), the logit baseline BL1$_\\text{easy}$ fires on 4 and the activation readout $N1$ fires on~1 (exact McNemar $b = 4$, $c = 1$, $p = 0.375$); this comparison is underpowered and not a definitive result.\n\nOn a broader pooled comparison across all 24 graded no-op edits, the geometric activation readout candidates (N1, N6 and their variants) produce zero false alarms while BL1 produces 11 false alarms (exact McNemar $p = 0.001$). This powered comparison confirms that the specificity advantage of mid-layer activation readouts over the logit baseline is statistically reliable.\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_specificity_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{False-alarm rate versus sensitivity for all 32 candidate readouts on the specificity panel. Each point is one readout; color indicates readout class (blue = activation, orange = logit, green = weight, red = text/card). Activation readouts cluster in the low-false-alarm region (0--3/15); logit baselines scatter across 5--8/15; the weight-space cosine B7 has the most false alarms (9/15). No readout achieves both zero false alarms and high sensitivity.}\n  \\label{fig:specificity}\n\\end{figure}\n\nThe logit-gap baseline fires on 6/15 (BL1$_\\text{easy}$) to 8/15 (BL1$_\\text{truelogit}$): int8 weight-only quantisation, system-prompt swaps and head-only unembedding edits all shift the final-layer logit gap without changing judged behaviour. The weight-space cosine B7 fires on 9/15 (every dtype cast produces a false alarm). Among text baselines, the greedy refusal rate fires on 2/15 and has the highest sensitivity (7/8 of evaluable effective pairs) but measures generated text rather than activations. AMS Tier-2 (the reference-based verify rule) achieves zero false alarms (0/15); however, this number partly reflects the fact that AMS scores were computed from a file-level reimplementation at batch size~1, which avoids the padding artefact described in Section~\\ref{sec:discussion}. AMS Tier-2 detects none of the 8 evaluable effective changes.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\scriptsize\n\\caption{All 32 candidate readouts. FA = false alarms on 15 no-ops (12 non-degenerate in parentheses). Sens = sensitivity on 9 effective pairs (denominator varies where noted). Disp = median null-SD displacement on no-ops. Readout class: \\textbf{A} = activation, \\textbf{L} = logit, \\textbf{W} = weight, \\textbf{T} = text/card.}\n\\label{tab:specificity}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcrrcr}\n\\toprule\n\\textbf{Readout} & \\textbf{Cl.} & \\textbf{FA/15 (12)} & \\textbf{Sens} & \\textbf{FA pairs} & \\textbf{Disp} \\\\\n\\midrule\nN1 ($d$ at $\\ell^*$) & A & 1 (1) & 5/9 & F3\\_dpo & 0.024 \\\\\nN1$_\\text{parentL}$ & A &
